title: Playing on top of the beat and each drummer's cymbal beat
summary: How different drummers play the cymbal beat and pair with different bass players.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I find that fascinating, this idea of playing on top of the beat. How can you — I heard Louis Hayes one night at some club and I said, “he is so on top of this beat, how does this music not speed up?” Or maybe it does.

Maybe it does. Well you see I don’t know, because each guy’s got a different cymbal beat. Like Jimmy Cobb, you would think he’d be playing quarter notes, but he’s actually playing a real tight sixteenth note. But you see what I did, the way, my father, when he first showed me the beat, he said, “this is the way the beat goes,” and he had to do it with two hands. But the way I practiced it was I would go [drums]. So if you play a flam [drums] then you’re not playing it right as far as I’m concerned. So it’s got to be [drums]. Rather than [drums]. Because the right stick is not where I hear the time. So it’s like the swinging thing. So like I always play it that way and then some guys just play straight quarter notes [drums] you know like that. And then there’s [drums]. And Cozy Cole almost played [drums]. I mean I never could quite figure that one out. But each guy’s got

their own cymbal beat. Louis Hayes, and each guy works differently, works better with certain bass players. Like Louis Hayes and Sam Jones hit it beautifully, and also Philly Joe Jones and Paul Chambers hit it beautifully. But Louis Hayes and Paul Chambers didn’t hit it as well, and Philly Joe didn’t hit it quite as well with Sam Jones. So everybody’s got their own time feel that works for them. Bass players, for me, I mean I’m very particular about bass players you know. And really, if I’m going to be able to be free — I know that if my arm starts to hurt I’m doing something — I’m trying to adjust to something. That’s just me.
